title: Can I Solve a 3600 ELO Puzzle?
summary: Tony solves chess.com puzzles filtered to narrow rating ranges (e.g. 100-110, 600-610) climbing in steps of 500 from 100 to 3600 Elo. Early ones are back-rank mates; he 'cheeses' 2100, gets the move order wrong at 3100 (~7:27), and on the 3600 puzzle finds the right ideas but misses the final move (Ne7 was correct, ~12:05).
rules: Standard chess puzzles: find the best move sequence for the side to move.
win_condition: Solve each puzzle correctly (meta goal: solve up to 3600).

opponent.name: chess.com puzzles (no opponent)
opponent.avatar_description: none; puzzle UI 'Black to Move' with star rating

setup: Puzzle positions (not standard start); e.g. one frame: White K,R,pawns vs Black K,Q,R,pawns, Black to move.
current_impl_issues: Impl 'puzzle' k=1 offers a single 'smothered mate' puzzle; video is a ladder of 8 rating tiers with real puzzle positions.
evidence: 0:01 'solve puzzles rated 100 Elo all the way up to 3,600'; 0:30/0:45/1:05/2:09/3:35/5:58 tier changes; 7:27 wrong move order; 12:52 'attempted puzzles all the way up to 3600'. Frame visual_b: puzzle UI.
not_playable_reason: Not a variant: solving standard chess.com puzzles at rising ratings (100, 600, 1100, 1600, 2100, 2600, 3100, 3600). Could be remade as a puzzle-ladder mode.
